correctness.rationale: Mori v1 Definition 3.1 makes the trivialization integral; Lemma 3.5 makes both the linear sum and the sum of squares invariant under positive refactorization. On the reference CY factorization both equal the length m. For a competitor this gives sum x_j=sum x_j^2=m, hence sum x_j(x_j-1)=0. Each x_j is an integer and x_j(x_j-1) is nonnegative with equality only at 0 and 1, forcing the asserted binary values and exact zero count. Mori v1 also gives factorization-independent rank V and the formulas b2=m-rank V and chi=2-d+m, yielding the stated topological defect equalities. The bundled finite checker only regresses the elementary integer implication; the proof is exact and infinite.

value.rationale: The result converts a coarse minimality theorem into an exact structural accounting law. Every extra positive factor in the same planar monodromy is forced into a single detectable class: it is annihilated by the reference CY trivialization, and each such null factor contributes exactly one to both the length and the b2/Euler-characteristic excess. This supplies a reusable obstruction and bookkeeping principle for positive substitutions and competing planar Stein fillings, rather than a routine restatement of the inequality.
